priorities.name: P9 (scope amendment) — nothing swings at nothing: a strike only lands when it has reached
priorities.check_method: Owner ruling: "There shouldn't be pretending to attack and not hitting anything." Three of the six ATTACKING-hold predicates were EXISTENCE checks with no notion of distance; the creature and bond STRIKE arms had no range gate at all. Creature and bond validity now share ONE reach predicate with their strike arms. The shape case is fixed at its source - the strike arm RELEASES targetPrimitiveId when out of reach so the creature re-seeks and walks in. Making primitiveValid reach-aware was BUILT, PROBED and REVERTED: a melee unit is frozen while ATTACKING and Helga walks, so she left a goblin's 35px reach on tick 34 and no moving defender would ever be killable in melee again. 4 fixtures that struck from outside their own reach were MOVED INTO range, not weakened. Verified: typecheck 0, vitest 4513/4513.

reflexion_entries_to_archive: P1 #the-ruling-was-24-sessions-old-and-never-built: R173 was RULED in S173 with a worked table and left unimplemented while the code ran DEF=n-1 and banked damage per-bond. The owner rediscovered it as a bug report. A ruling with no implementation and no carry-forward is indistinguishable from a ruling that was never given.

P1 #one-ladder-preserved-the-balance-it-was-feared-to-break: moving shapes from a 1000-point scale onto attackFifths was expected to retune everything. Measured, it preserved drone-fells-shape-in-3 and Ra-one-shots exactly, and moved ONE relationship (suicide 3->4 blasts). The fear was worth measuring rather than trusting.

P5 #his-diagnosis-was-wrong-and-his-observation-was-right: he said the bags had too much health; they had the minimum possible. But his SIX SECONDS was exact - it was the bag expiry timer running out while an army swung and missed. Take the observation as data and re-derive the cause.

P4 #the-window-i-added-to-be-safe-was-the-defect: both TV clips failed check-clip on edge-touching frames, so I capped sampleWindow. That cut each clip off MID-EXPLOSION and the row's held last frame became a frozen blast instead of the settled state. Measuring which frames actually offended (spawning 51-53, destroyed 59-60) showed 12-of-96 is stride 8 and never samples them - the cap was never needed. Caught ONLY by auditioning the packed sheet on the dark board, which is why that step is in the protocol.

P9 #a-probe-beats-an-argument: making primitiveValid reach-aware is the obvious completion of the owner's rule and I could argue either way for twenty minutes. A six-predicate probe of the real host tick answered it in one run: Helga steps out of a goblin's 35px reach on tick 34 while he is frozen in ATTACKING, so every moving defender would have become unkillable in melee. Built, measured, reverted - and the shape mime killed at its source instead.
P3 #the-change-that-could-not-possibly-do-anything: setting lifetimeTicks on a config whose persistent:true overrides it. Caught only by reading the factory it came from. Same shape as S153 P1.

P10 #the-constraint-that-forbade-the-obvious-fix: the die clip blew the 8192 texture ceiling, and dropping one frame was the obvious answer - until a test showed attack.frames x ticksPerFrame must EQUAL the attack cadence, so 20 x 3 is forced and the cell is capped at 409 instead. The fix had to move to the ART (land compact), not the frame count. Two constraints crossing is where a cheap fix usually hides a real one.

analyze.promotion_candidates_reviewed: Boot surfaced three ADVISORY reflexion patterns (>=3x). Reviewed, NOT auto-codified, per the constitution. (1) #empirical-refutes-plausible-criticals (9x) - STRONGLY reinforced this session and now the dominant pattern in the log: the $6.20 verdict, the 'stuck animation' diagnosis and check-clip's idle PASS were all plausible and all wrong, each refuted by one measurement. (2) #raw-code-not-abbreviations (6x) - reinforced: reading check-clip.mjs's actual detector, rather than its summary output, is what exposed the false pass, and reading build-sprite-atlas.mjs is what showed framesPerState has no per-state override. (3) #policy-not-instance (4x) - the honest counter-example this session. I fixed THIS fog assertion but did not build anything that would catch the NEXT renderer added to fogHiddenLayer. RECOMMENDATION for a future META PDR, deliberately not actioned here (out of scope, and the owner is budget-constrained): a gate that fails when a renderer is constructed with a shared parent layer but is absent from fog.spec.ts's roll call. That converts the project's most-repeated display-list defect from prose into enforcement. Do NOT add it without its own PDR.
what_went_right: The S161 rule was applied correctly for the first time under real pressure: 4/4 lanes died and every one was re-run by hand rather than filed as 'the sweep produced nothing'.
Committing and pushing per priority meant the spend-limit interruption and the weekly-budget squeeze cost nothing - P1 was already live when P2 started.

The owner's mid-session ruling (20 frames) was absorbed as a scope amendment WITH its companion change (ticksPerFrame rescaled) rather than shipped half-done - the S175 P1c lesson, applied unprompted.
A defect was found in work I had already committed (the health bar's padded cell) and fixed before the owner saw it.
what_to_do_differently: RE-READ EVERY GATE AT CLOSE, not only at boot. A boot reading measures the session before yours. This is the single highest-value change and it is what hid a red CI for four commits.
Dispatch fan-out lanes as SEPARATE invocations. Three sessions have now lost an entire sweep to one spend limit; the cost of splitting is a few seconds.
Read exit codes from a captured $? at EVERY site, including the ones that feel like bookkeeping. I quoted this rule to the owner and then broke it on the review gate in the same session.
